zh: 每个全 1 正方形都有唯一的右下角。所以可以对每个格子问：以它为右下角的全 1 正方形，边长最大是多少？所有格子答案中的最大值就是题目要的边长（不是面积）。
设 dp[r][c] 为以 (r,c) 为右下角的最大全 1 正方形边长。格子为 0 时 dp=0；为 1 时，一个边长 s 的正方形去掉底行或右列，会分别包含以上方、左方、左上方为右下角的边长 s−1 的正方形，因此 dp[r][c]=1+min(上, 左, 左上)，并且这个值确实能取到。逐行计算只依赖上一行和本行左边，用一维滚动数组即可。

读入 n（n=0 直接输出 0），开长度 n+1 的数组 dp，全为 0。逐行逐列读格子：先记下旧的 dp[col]（即“上方”），若格子为 1 则 dp[col]=1+min(旧 dp[col], dp[col−1], diagonal)，否则置 0；更新答案后令 diagonal=上方旧值，供下一列作“左上”。每行开始时 diagonal=0。输入可达 32MiB，应边读边算、不保存整个矩阵。
en: Every all-1 square has a unique bottom-right corner. So for each cell, ask: what is the largest side of an all-1 square whose bottom-right corner is this cell? The maximum over all cells is the side length the problem asks for (not the area).

Let dp[r][c] be the largest side of an all-1 square with bottom-right corner (r,c). For a 0 cell dp=0; for a 1 cell, a square of side s with its bottom row or right column removed contains squares of side s−1 ending at the cell above, the cell to the left and the upper-left cell, so dp[r][c]=1+min(above, left, upper-left), and this value is actually achievable. Each row depends only on the previous row and the cells to its left in the current row, so a one-dimensional rolling array is enough.

Read n (if n=0, print 0 right away) and allocate an array dp of length n+1 filled with 0. Read the cells row by row and column by column: first remember the old dp[col] (the cell above); if the cell is 1, set dp[col]=1+min(old dp[col], dp[col−1], diagonal), otherwise set it to 0; update the answer, then set diagonal to that old value above so it serves as the upper-left for the next column. Reset diagonal to 0 at the start of each row. The input can reach 32MiB, so compute while reading instead of storing the whole matrix.

explanationEn:
## Recovering the fixed source and disclosing ranges

fastprep/FactSet/factset-largest-square-of-1s.md at the fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc explicitly says two-dimensional square matrix and describes the input as n lines with n integers each. The earlier curation truncated the text after an HTML less-than sign, which is no reason to conclude that the square-matrix structure is missing. The input of this problem is an n×n square matrix of 0s and 1s, where 1 marks a defective product; find the largest side length of a contiguous square submatrix consisting entirely of 1s — not the area, and not an arbitrary selection of rows and columns.

The original text gives no numeric upper bound on n. This site does not pretend that the original problem has a limit such as n≤1000, and instead supports every valid square matrix within the existing 32MiB per-case standard input budget. The first line of input gives n, followed by n lines with n whitespace-separated 0/1 values each; every line ends with a newline. The most compact usual encoding needs at least 2n² bytes plus the first line, so the order-4095 tests already sit right next to the current budget; 4095 is not an additionally declared original bound. Allowing n=0 and returning 0 is this site's explicit mathematical extension to the empty matrix and cannot be attributed to a guarantee of the original text. A non-empty all-0 matrix also returns 0.

The three public cases keep the original inputs and answers 3, 2, 1 exactly. Original example 1 writes the end of the 3×3 region starting at (0,0) as (3,3), which is a half-open bottom-right endpoint; this site uniformly uses the inclusive endpoint (2,2) instead, and the other two squares correspond to (3,2) and (4,2). The (1,1) in original example 2 is already an inclusive endpoint, and the two conventions must not be mixed. The image path on the author's machine is inaccessible and is not used as additional evidence; all results are computed independently from the readable matrices.

## Approach

Read the elements row by row. dp[col] is the largest side of an all-1 square whose bottom-right corner is that cell, for positions of the previous row or positions of the current row that have already been updated. When the current value is 0, set it to 0; when it is 1, take the minimum of the three side lengths above, to the left and to the upper-left, plus 1. Before updating, save the old value above, to serve as the upper-left of the next cell. The maximum over all positions is the answer.

## Proof of correctness

When the current cell is 0, no all-1 square can have it as its bottom-right corner, so the largest side is 0. When the current cell is 1, let the three neighboring subproblem values be a, b and c. Any candidate square of side s≥2, after removing its bottom row, its rightmost column and so on, contains the squares of side s−1 whose bottom-right corners are those three cells, so s≤1+min(a,b,c). Conversely, each of the three neighboring positions has an all-1 square of side d=min(a,b,c), and their union together with the current cell covers a whole block of side d+1, so the upper bound is achieved. Side 1 also holds.

By induction in row and column order, the recurrence always produces the correct current side length. In the rolling array, the value above being read has not been overwritten yet, the value to the left has already been updated, and the saved diagonal is the previous row's left value, so the implementation matches the recurrence. Every all-1 square has a unique bottom-right corner, so enumerating all cells and taking the maximum covers every candidate and outputs the global maximum side length.

## Complexity and transmission budget

Time O(n²), extra space O(n); standard input is read as a stream and the full matrix is not stored. The empty-matrix extension takes O(1) time. Under the input budget, n and the dp values stay far below the signed 32-bit limit; the output is a single side-length integer. The reference uses C++20, and the package allows 3 seconds/256MiB with 64KiB of output. Other languages must still meet the same time and memory limits. Local performance records cannot replace acceptance in the Linux sandbox.

## Independent verification

The small oracle enumerates every starting point and every side length and directly checks all cells of that region, without calling the DP. All 531 binary square matrices with n=0..3 are enumerated exhaustively, and the native reference is actually run on 163 unique inputs. Medium matrices use two-dimensional prefix sums, enumerating squares from the largest side downward and checking the area sum, independently of the maximum-square DP.

Two 4095×4095 matrices of 33538055 bytes each: all 1s, expecting 4095, and a checkerboard, expecting 1 (every 2×2 contains a 0). These two use independent closed forms and do not build huge two-dimensional Python integer objects; the reference is actually run on each and its peak memory on this machine is measured. Other boundary cases cover all zeros, an isolated 1, a missing diagonal, borders, interior holes, stripes, offset squares and dense random matrices. Three negative controls return the area, omit the diagonal condition and count only the first row, respectively; they count as valid kills only if they exit normally on all official inputs.
